newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ministers approve law on foreign banks.
newsitem.headline: German ministers approve law on foreign banks.

text.p: German state finance ministers agreed on Thursday to leave unchanged their tax burden on foreign banks, accepting the argument that an increase would spark an exodus.
The state of Hesse, home to the German financial capital Frankfurt, said the ministers agreed by a 10-4 vote, with two abstentions, to maintain the current tax rate.
Foreign banks have long been taxed 0.25 to two percent on business done in Germany.
All 16 German states except Hesse had sought earlier in the year to raise the tax on branches of foreign banks in Germany.
But Hesse, backed by Frankfurt officials, fought against change, saying thousands of jobs were in danger because foreign banks threatened to shut their German operations.
